channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Jaywick Sands' Brooklands could be rebuilt as one-way road with beach path
item.description: Tendring District Council has a preferred plan for the pothole-hit private road in Jaywick Sands, which residents named as their top priority for investment, but no decision has been taken.

item.title: Essex all-rounder Luc Benkenstein leaves for Durham
item.description: The leg-spinner has left by mutual agreement after 80 appearances across all formats since joining in 2021.

item.title: Essex Police arrest 17 in week-long county lines crackdown
item.description: Eleven people were charged and remanded, and officers seized 22 throwing blades, a zombie knife, drugs and cash.

item.title: Harlow employment rate rises to 82.9% in latest ONS figures
item.description: Harlow is among the five best-performing areas in the country for jobs growth, according to Your Harlow's report on official labour market data.

item.title: Harlow's River Way Bridge to shut to all vehicles
item.description: The River Way Bridge in Harlow is to close fully to traffic, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Lakeside Retail Park to open King Living furniture showroom on Saturday
item.description: The family-owned Australian sofa and furniture maker is opening a two-floor store at West Thurrock, aimed at shoppers across Essex and east London.

item.title: Braintree MP James Cleverly to run for London mayor for Conservatives
item.description: Sir James Cleverly took 86% of the vote in a ballot of London Conservative members and will not seek reselection in his Braintree seat at the next general election.

item.title: Southend homelessness charity HARP launches Christmas Unwrapped appeal
item.description: HARP is asking people and businesses in Southend and south Essex to give towards festive meals, gifts and treats for people experiencing homelessness this Christmas.

item.title: Stansted owner's survey puts east ahead for export growth
item.description: Six in 10 exporters in the East of England, which includes Essex, grew overseas sales between July and September, the best of four regions in a survey commissioned by London Stansted's owner MAG.

item.title: Wivenhoe Town to take out pitchside brick walls under new FA safety rules
item.description: Wivenhoe Town is replacing the brick walls around its pitch after the FA banned solid barriers at non-league grounds following the death of former Arsenal youth player Billy Vigar, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: London Gateway systems fault queues lorries back to A13 Manorway
item.description: Link roads in Stanford-le-Hope and Corringham backed up as trucks waited to get into the DP World port in Thurrock.

item.title: Saffron Walden opens nominations for Freedom of the town
item.description: Saffron Walden Town Council is inviting nominations for residents who have made an exceptional, lasting contribution to the town's life, wellbeing, reputation or development.

item.title: Harlow Council plans tougher line on landlords who let unsafe homes
item.description: Harlow tenants living with damp, mould or missing smoke alarms would see the council move straight to formal action against their landlords under a new policy.

item.title: Essex training boss calls Milburn youth jobs review a 'missed opportunity'
item.description: Chris Hodson of Pitman Training in Essex blames wage rates, employment taxes and welfare, not a shortage of job schemes, for young people being out of work.

item.title: Basildon Council heads for £3.8m overspend as homelessness costs rise
item.description: Repairs and damp and mould work also leave Basildon's council housing account forecast to finish £3.2m over budget in 2026/27, according to a report for the council's Cabinet.

item.title: Maldon council expects 5 planning appeals this year costing about £500,000
item.description: Maldon District Council's day-to-day spending is close to budget overall, with a forecast overspend of £126,000, or 0.9%, for 2026/27, its Director of Finance reports.

item.title: Maldon council proposes new rules for selling its land and buildings
item.description: Community groups wanting to take over a Maldon District Council building or plot would have to show public benefit, local support and sound finances under the draft policy.

item.title: Chelmsford's Sandon School raffles prizes to keep GTA 6 fans in class
item.description: A secondary school near Chelmsford is entering pupils who attend into a prize draw, after the long-awaited video game's UK release.

item.title: Essex Wildlife Trust aims to raise £1m for nature in three-year appeal
item.description: The county's wildlife charity will use its Christmas appeal to start raising money for habitats, species and waterways across Essex as it nears its 70th birthday.

item.title: Thurrock Council may stop buying new mobile phones for staff
item.description: Thurrock Council could halt purchases of new staff mobile phones as part of its budget savings proposals, the Yellow Advertiser reports.

item.title: Chelmsford to dip to 1C on Friday night before heavy rain on Sunday
item.description: The Met Office forecast for Chelmsford shows a cloudy, damp Thursday, a near-freezing night to follow on Friday and the wettest, windiest day of the week on Sunday.

item.title: Southend council leadership challenge fails by two votes
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council's leader keeps the post after a narrow vote, the Yellow Advertiser reports.

item.title: Brentwood Town edge Burgess Hill Town 1-0 in Isthmian Premier
item.description: Brentwood Town, who had taken one point from their previous four matches, climb out of the Isthmian Premier Division's bottom four.

item.title: Church Langley man, 51, gets suspended term over attempts to incite children
item.description: A Harlow man was given a 20-month prison sentence, suspended for two years, at Chelmsford Crown Court for offences against children under 16 in Harlow in 2025.

item.title: BAE Systems, with Great Baddow base, plans up to 1,070 UK job cuts
item.description: The defence company says the cuts will fall on its UK head office and air sector, out of about 50,000 UK employees.

item.title: Driver jailed for 81mph Theydon Bois crash that killed pedestrian
item.description: A North Weald man who lost control of his car on the B172 Abridge Road near Theydon Bois, killing a 59-year-old Basildon man walking at the roadside, has been jailed for six years and nine months.

item.title: Harlow's William Aylmer tops list of cheapest Wetherspoons in the east
item.description: A price comparison has found that a basket of 50 food and drink items costs less at The William Aylmer in Harlow than at any other Wetherspoon pub in the East of England.

item.title: Air ambulance charity recruits 27 volunteer responders for Essex
item.description: Essex & Herts Air Ambulance has taken on a new team of volunteers to give potentially lifesaving treatment at the scene of some of the most serious emergencies in Essex.

item.title: Southend small firms told of 75% discount on Cyber Essentials certificate
item.description: SAVS Southend is pointing small charities and businesses to the government's Cyber Essentials First Step Fund, which cuts the cost of the cyber security certificate.

item.title: Colchester Institute students serve breakfast at Essex business festival
item.description: Hospitality and professional cookery students from Colchester Institute fed delegates at the Essex Chambers of Commerce Festival of Business at Braxted Park.

item.title: Purfleet lorry park refused by Thurrock councillors goes to appeal
item.description: Developers want the Planning Inspectorate to overturn the refusal of 24-hour HGV and container storage on the former vehicle testing site in Tank Hill Road, Purfleet-on-Thames.

item.title: Billericay community awards draw more than 20,000 public votes
item.description: Cloud 9 Espresso Bar, the High Street Post Office and volunteer Mark Thomas were among 10 winners named at Billericay's second community awards.

item.title: Saffron Walden lights switch-on brings Market Place party on Friday
item.description: Father Christmas will switch on Saffron Walden's Christmas lights at 6pm on Friday 20 November, with music, food stalls and pantomime cast members in the Market Place from 3pm.

item.title: Colchester deputy leader criticises £900 SEND school transport charges
item.description: Colchester City Council's deputy leader says the cost of getting students with special educational needs to school or college is adding to the pressure on their families, as a review of the charges goes on.

item.title: Harlow Council spoofs GTA 6 with video tour of its town centre revamp
item.description: A day before Grand Theft Auto VI goes on sale, Harlow Council has released a tongue-in-cheek video that drives viewers round the town's roundabouts and rebuilt Market Square.

item.title: Colchester to get US chicken chain Raising Cane's first UK drive-thru
item.description: Colchester is one of four new UK sites named by the American fried chicken chain, with the restaurant due to open in 2028.

item.title: Southend seafront to get new public toilets in £750,000 plan
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet has backed the spending, which comes from outside the council, after a review of the city's public toilets.

item.title: University of Essex may house 150 MoD staff in spare Colchester rooms
item.description: Spare rooms on the Colchester campus could go to Ministry of Defence personnel, BBC News reports.

item.title: Essex water firm adds 30% more leak crews as reservoirs stay low
item.description: Essex & Suffolk Water says supplies across mid and south Essex are not at risk, but wants customers to keep saving water through the winter while the hosepipe ban stays in place.

item.title: Roydon narrowboat gutted by fire on River Lee near Dobbs Weir Road
item.description: About 20 firefighters tackled a fire that left a narrowboat fully alight on the River Lee at Roydon, with nobody on board.

item.title: Billericay Town hold Truro City to goalless draw in Cornwall
item.description: Billericay Town stay sixth in the National League South after taking a point in wet and windy conditions against one of the division's front-runners.

item.title: Epping pupils and Speed Watch volunteers join Vision Zero road safety day
item.description: Pupils challenged speeding drivers and Community Speed Watch volunteers checked traffic in their own streets during a Vision Zero operation in Epping, the Safer Essex Roads Partnership says.

item.title: Wickford sisters' Shotgate craft fair raises money for cancer and pet charities
item.description: Cancer Research and the PDSA are the beneficiaries of the latest Shotgate Gift & Crafts Fair in Wickford.

item.title: Epping job fair draws more than 300 people hoping to work in tourism
item.description: Epping Forest District Council says jobseekers met employers including Stansted Airport, Jet2 and the Epping Ongar Railway at its Civic Offices event.

item.title: Harlow College shuts for the day after power cut
item.description: Students at Harlow College's Velizy Avenue campus were told to stay away because the site had lost its electricity supply.

item.title: Shoebury toddler Blake, 17 months, remembered as police inquiry continues
item.description: Blake Branch died after ambulance crews raised concerns for a child's welfare at a Shoeburyness home in October. Detectives investigating his death have two people on conditional bail.

item.title: Southend cabinet backs investment partnership for Better Queensway
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council's long-running plan to rebuild the Queensway area moves on to its next stage.

item.title: Southend's Palace Hotel to switch from Radisson to IHG's Garner brand
item.description: The Southend hotel, which trades as the Park Inn Palace, can already be booked on IHG's website as an independent property.

item.title: Little Havens shows bereaved children's grief artwork in Thundersley
item.description: Havens Hospices is displaying 'My Invisible Backpack', pictures made by children it supports, for Children's Grief Awareness Week.

item.title: South Ockendon school trust keeps pupils' Christmas events as it reviews visits
item.description: The Catalyst Academies Trust, which runs Benyon Primary and five other Thurrock schools, says it is close to new arrangements that would let more relatives attend Christmas performances.

item.title: Ongar's Mulberry House named best wedding venue in East of England
item.description: The High Ongar venue won the regional Wedding Venue of the Year title at The Wedding Industry Awards 2027, Your Harlow reports.

item.title: Basildon jobless claims climb to 4,600, highest in Essex
item.description: Basildon now has more people claiming work-related benefits than any other Essex district, with St Martin's ward the worst affected at 6.3% of working-age residents.

item.title: M11 southbound reopens near Stansted after two-lorry crash
item.description: National Highways has reopened the motorway between Duxford and Bishop's Stortford, ending a closure of about 25 hours that sent drivers heading into Essex on a long detour through Hertfordshire.

item.title: Maldon planners set to decide on 159 homes north of West Street in Tollesbury at a third meeting
item.description: Maldon District Council's Planning Committee returns on Wednesday 25 November 2026 to an outline plan for up to 159 homes and a new road in Tollesbury, after deferring it in August and October.

item.title: Complaints from Basildon council tenants fell by nearly a fifth last year, but most are still about repairs
item.description: Basildon Council's Housing Services received 759 first-stage complaints in 2025/26, 19.5% fewer than the year before, according to a report for the Housing Scrutiny Committee on Wednesday 25 November 2026.

item.title: Thurrock Council looks for £27.3m of cuts, with 72 jobs in line to go
item.description: Thurrock Council's Reform UK leadership wants savings over two years to balance a budget in which a quarter of spending goes on debt interest.

item.title: Clacton Pier keeps its big new ride for spring 2027 under wraps
item.description: Clacton Pier is investing in a major new ride, known for now only by the code name Project Rock, which is due to open in spring 2027.

item.title: Tillingham villagers divided over Home Office plan to house six asylum seekers
item.description: Residents of the Dengie peninsula village are split over the plan, with concerns raised about transport and local services.

item.title: Grays-raised Russell Brand faces move to third prison over YouTube message
item.description: The comedian, who grew up in Grays, is under a Ministry of Justice investigation after his wife read out a statement from him on the couple's YouTube show.

item.title: Whatever happened to Loughton's £2bn data centre?
item.description: It was originally due to open before the end of 2026. Instead Microsoft has pulled out, the electricity is years away and Nscale has no new date for its AI site.
